analysis: The closest response deliberately spans three domains. Biodiversity introduces observation and classification, followed by conservation biology and climate science. Governance and ethics connect science to social choices. Statistics, qualitative inquiry, documentary and historical research support the programme-wide inquiry goal. UCR has no common annually sequenced project line or required thesis in these schedules.

The sciences response joins molecular biology, physiology, biochemistry and immunology to neuroscience, behaviour and disease. The first-semester gateway precedes the only planned offering of Psycholinguistics. Philosophy of Mind provides conceptual synthesis late in the degree. Experimental methods precede evidence synthesis. There is no technical AI sequence in this option.

The social sciences option combines legal institutions, politics and economic analysis with finance, entrepreneurship, transnational business law and an economic study of AI. The business gateway precedes Transnational Business Law. Economics and governance dominate over a specialist global supply-chain or management programme.

Each distinct route differs substantially in coursework. Courses with only broad or thematic connections remain course-only; elective placeholders do not warrant an individual equivalent. Optional independent research stays outside the scheduled credits.
constructionStop: Three coherent, distinct options reach the programme limit.

HCBCOGN312.contribution: examines the psychological and neural processes of human language production and comprehension
HCBCOGN312.topics: Psycholinguistics is the study of the neurobiological and psychological factors that enable us to acquire, use, and understand language. Modern research draws on cognitive psychology, neuroscience, and computer science to investigate how language is processed. The course focuses primarily, though not exclusively, on the neuroscience of language. Students examine theoretical and experimental issues in speech production and comprehension, language impairments, the relationship between thought and language, and the evolution and acquisition of language. They also gain hands-on experience with experimental approaches to the study of language and develop an understanding of human linguistic capacity as a subject of multidisciplinary research. Topics covered: What is language? Evolutionary aspects of language and animal communication; language and thought; aphasia; language acquisition; bilingualism; speech comprehension; semantics; reading and dyslexia; speech production.
